chunks: And if you could see when they are placed before their Lord, He will say, 'Is not this the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny.'

key_terms.فَذُوقُوا: then taste (imperative, often used for experiencing punishment or pleasure)
key_terms.وُقِفُوا: stood/placed (in a specific context, usually before a judge or authority)

ai.seo_question: What happens when disbelievers are presented before Allah on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-An'am, this verse highlights the moment of ultimate clarity where disbelievers, previously blinded by arrogance, are forced to acknowledge the truth of divine revelation before it is too late. Shia exegetes often contrast this with the concept of 'fitrah' (innate disposition), noting that while the truth becomes undeniable in the Hereafter, the opportunity for voluntary acceptance has passed. This scene serves as a poignant reminder that denial was a choice made in life, not a lack of evidence in the afterlife.
